title: In-Situ Polarimetry in Collimated Magneto-Infrared Spectroscopy System
authors: Zeping Shi, Wenbin Wu, Zhiwei Zhang, Yuhan Du, Chenyao Xu, Congming Hao, Xiangyu Jiang, Xin Chen, Guangyi Wang, Mingsen Zhou, Chunhui Pan, Wei Lu, Hao Shen, Haifeng Pan, Zhenrong Sun, Junhao Chu, Xiang Yuan
abstract: Magneto-infrared spectroscopy under strong magnetic fields provides a powerful probe of Landau quantization and field-induced collective excitations, yet its full potential has long been constrained by the lack of in-situ polarization control, because the highly divergent infrared beam propagating through narrow light tubes undergoes multiple wall reflections, leading to severe polarization degradation. Here we report a collimated magneto-infrared spectroscopy system that integrates continuous in-situ polarimetry. The system employs incident and exit collimation chambers forming a Kepler type optical architecture, which converts the large-aperture FTIR output into a low-divergence beam and strongly suppresses multi-reflection trajectories inside long gold-plated light tubes, thereby enhancing both optical throughput and polarization fidelity. A remotely controlled polarization module, consisting of an automated linear polarizer and a switchable Fresnel rhomb positioned entirely outside the high-field region, enables continuous in-situ tuning between linear, circular, and arbitrary elliptical polarization states without thermal cycling, manual realignment, or breaking vacuum. Interchangeable compact focusing modules further support Faraday and Voigt geometries in both transmission and reflection experiments within a 50 mm magnet bore, providing efficient beam focusing and signal collection while maintaining polarization fidelity. The setup achieves a minimum root-mean-square noise of 0.0033%, an average noise of 0.0082%, and a linear polarization extinction ratio up to 40:1. We demonstrate the capability through continuous in-situ linear polarimetry and broadband circular polarimetry in the magneto-infrared spectroscopy of various single crystals. This platform establishes a robust experimental framework for in-situ polarization-resolved magneto-infrared spectroscopy.
summary: The paper introduces a sophisticated magneto-infrared spectroscopy system featuring in-situ polarimetry capabilities. By employing specialized collimation optics, the setup overcomes polarization degradation caused by light reflections within high-field cryostats. This allows for continuous, quantitative measurements of polarization-dependent spectral features essential for studying quantum phenomena in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The full potential of magneto-infrared spectroscopy for probing Landau quantization is limited by the lack of continuous, in-situ polarization control due to severe polarization degradation from beam reflections.
main_result: The authors report a novel collimated system that achieves high polarization fidelity (extinction ratio up to 40:1) and enables continuous in-situ linear and circular polarimetry measurements under strong magnetic fields.
method: They designed an optical architecture using incident and exit Kepler type collimation chambers coupled with a remotely controlled polarization module outside the high-field region.
model_or_system: The platform integrates an FTIR spectrometer, superconducting magnet (up to 12 T), and interchangeable focusing modules supporting Faraday/Voigt geometries for transmission and reflection experiments within a small bore.
key_observables: Linear polarization extinction ratio ($\ge 40:1$), minimum root-mean-square noise ($\le 0.0033\%$), and polarization-dependent spectral signatures (e.g., $C_2$ symmetry).
important_parameters: Magnetic field strength up to 12 T; sample bore diameter of $\approx 50 	ext{ mm}$; low temperature regime ($\approx 1.7 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that collimating the beam and suppressing multi-reflections significantly enhances polarization fidelity compared to conventional direct focusing.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the overall system schematic, detailed designs of incident/exit collimation chambers, operational modes (linear/circular polarization), and performance metrics like extinction ratio vs. aperture size.
paper_structure: The paper details the necessity for in-situ polarimetry, presents the novel Kepler-type optical design to suppress reflections, describes the modular components (focusing modules, polarization optics), and concludes with demonstrations of continuous measurements in both linear and circular polarization modes.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly advanced experimental platform for measuring fundamental material properties related to electron band structure and magnetoelectric coupling under extreme conditions, which is crucial input for theoretical models of correlated electronic states.
